games.title: Demonbane Chronicle
games.authors: 通宵虫 (Allnighter) and 南方小鬼 (South Imp), with the BBK Game Team
games.blurb: The best-known RPG of the BBK dictionary scene. Liu Qingfeng and his companions take on a rising tide of demons in a full-length turn-based adventure with towns, dungeons, Taoist magic and a long story, all on a 159×96 one-bit screen.

games.title: Heroes of Jin Yong
games.blurb: A fan-made wuxia crossover on the BBKRPG engine: pick a hero, join one of a dozen sects from Shaolin to the Ancient Tomb, learn their martial arts, and travel between the Capital, Xixia, Dali and Yangzhou alongside Guo Jing, Huang Rong, Linghu Chong and other Jin Yong heroes.

games.title: Heroes' Altar
games.authors: 才子工作室 (Caizi Studio): 金远见 (Jin Yuanjian), 柴梓 (Chai Zi)
games.blurb: A tongue-in-cheek wuxia fan game on the BBKRPG engine: a modern kid switches on a time machine and wakes up as a fourteen-year-old in Safehaven, then joins a sect, forges gear, trains in a MUD-style sandbox and collects six sect heads' tokens to lure out the Archdemon, with plenty of fourth-wall jokes along the way.

games.title: Cross Entry
games.blurb: A one-person fantasy RPG on the BBKRPG engine: two thousand years after humankind was banished underground, the foundling swordswoman Eluna, sure she came from the surface, drags the reluctant crown prince Delat across four cities after the four Crests that open the legendary Cross Entry.

games.title: Three Kingdoms: Hegemony
games.authors: BBK Game Group; code by 通宵虫 (Allnighter) and 南方小鬼 (South Imp), art by Sunday
games.blurb: BBK's own turn-based Three Kingdoms strategy game. Pick one of four eras and a warlord, then run your cities month by month - farming, trade, diplomacy and recruitment - and fight tactical battles with officers, troop types and skills to unify the realm.

games.title: Ode to Gallantry
games.authors: 纯蓝工作室 (Chunlan Studio): 纯蓝守护者 (Chunlan Guardian), SSK
games.blurb: A cheeky wuxia raising sim on the BBKRPG engine: as young Mo Ming you age a year for every hour of play, join and climb a sect, win the Martial Tournament, marry, found your own sect and storm Bright Peak, then seal the world's demons in a well with an array of BBK electronic dictionaries. Not Jin Yong's novel, despite the name.
games.content_note: This fan game, written around 2005, has a side area on a "Japan Island" built on crude anti-Japanese jokes: the player spits on and kicks a Japanese official, and refusing ends the game for "shaming China". The jokes come from their moment. In spring 2005 Japan's bid for a permanent UN Security Council seat, together with Japanese history textbooks that played down wartime atrocities and prime-ministerial visits to the Yasukuni Shrine, set off mass protests across China, and that anger filled the Chinese teenage forums this game came from. Behind it lies the memory of Japan's invasion and occupation of China (1931-1945). The translation keeps these scenes as written but not the slur 小日本 ("little Japan"), which becomes "the Japanese". The game also has its teenage authors' swearing and crude humour.
